newsitem.title: CHINA: China Aerospace eyes role in satellite project.
newsitem.headline: China Aerospace eyes role in satellite project.

text.p: Hong Kong-listed China Aerospace International Holdings Ltd is hoping to take part in a project for a direct satellite broadcasting system in China, chairman and president Wang Meiyue said on Monday.
China Aerospace International, a subsidiary of Beijing's state-owned China Aerospace Corp, hoped to have a role in the project, including the manufacture of ground receiving equipment, Wang said.
The project is currently being studied by Chinese authorities but Wang declined to say how likely an approval would be or when it might be made.
Wang said that if the project went ahead, there would be various partners, possibly including foreign interests, and that it would require investment of more than $600 million.
China Aerospace International hopes to be the main producer of 18-inch satellite receivers, which would be sold at about $300 each.
The company already manufactures such receivers and expects to produce about 30,000 of them by the end of the year. All of those are currently being exported.
The project would require satellite uplink facilities and some arrangement for programming.

Wang did not say who would handle which aspect of the project, but he said any such plan would have to include the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television and the State Science and Technology Commission.

He did not give any indication of earnings that might be anticipated from the project. He also did not say how China Aerospace International would finance its share but he said the company would be able to borrow if necessary.
China has in the past restricted sales of satellite dishes for the domestic market and any venture aimed at this market will face some political obstacles, analysts say.
